newsitem.title: GHANA: Ashanti stays on course for output target.
newsitem.headline: Ashanti stays on course for output target.

text.p: Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd says it is well protected against the current low world gold price and expects to meet its 1.1 million ounce production and cost forecast for 1997.
Ashanti said core capital expenditure programmes at key mines at Obuasi, Bibiani and Sanguiri were well on track, in a statement on Wednesday on operations for the first half of the year,.

The mining company, with a presence in 12 African countries, said the second quarter production of 281,980 ounces at a cash cost of $269 per ounce, brings the half-year total to 571,795 ounces at a reduced cash cost of $265 per ounce.
"Given the higher production forecast for the second half, Ashanti remains confident that the 1997 objective to produce 1.1 million ounces at $265 per ounce will be met," it said.
Construction work at Babiani in Ghana and Siguiri in Guinea is progressing well. Indications are that both projects will be completed on budget and on schedule, the statement added.
In Tanzania, Ashanti has more than doubled the Geita resource estimate to three million ounces and commenced a feasibility study.
At Obuasi, output of 203,811 ounces for the second quarter brought the total for the first half to 417,048 ounces or 99.3 percent of targeted production.
The statement said operating costs at Obuasi for the second quarter were $277 per ounce, slightly higher than the first quarter because of the lower gold output.
This brings costs at Obuasi for the year to date to an average of $274 per ounce, in line with the company's forecast for 1997 as a whole, it said.
It attributed an average of $6 per ounce of the cost to date to ore stockpiles, including the revaluation of the stockpiles to reflect the lower gold price.
A major cost reduction measure at Obuasi was the completion of a voluntary severance programme, which reduced the workforce by 800 or eight percent.

A charge of $2.5 million was taken as an exceptional item in the quarter and a further $0.6 million will be charged in the third quarter. The payback on these costs is estimated at 18 months, the statement said.
The annualised underground ore production rate for the first half was 1.9 million tonnes per annum, at a grade of 8.10 G/T.
In line with plans, surface mining operations have been significantly curtailed, from 36 million tonnes of ore and waste mined in the first half of 1996 to 16 million tonnes in 1997.
The statement said that at Ayanfuri, gold production for the half year of 29,062 ounces was higher than planned and 17 percent over that in 1996, mainly due to higher grade.
Operating costs at $223 per ounce were lower as a result of increased production but were offset by a higher rate of mining.
Total material mined rose by 35 percent to 3.3 million tonnes due to the need to build an ore stockpile to minimise the impact of the wet season on the operations, as occurred in 1996.
Ore stacked was marginally higher than the previous year at 643.000 tonnes at 1.67 G/T.
The full impact of the low grade heap leach operation at Iduapriem boosted gold output for the quarter to 39.734 ounces.

This brought the total for the half year to 74,646 ounces or 31 percent more than in 1996. The cash cost for Iduapriem for the first half was $256 per ounce, 18 percent lower than $311 per ounce in 1996.
Ashanti said gold production at its Freda-Rebecca mine for the half year of 51,039 ounces at a cost of $234 per ounce was seven percent higher than that in 1996, in line with forecasts.

Underground ore production from the Rebecca increased by 11 percent to 346,000 tonnes, at a higher grade of 3.12 G/T while the development of its underground mine to supplement ore supply when the open pits are phased out, is progressing, it said.
